comments.value: Your single thread performance is not good enough for VRChat. AMD did a good job on Ryzen but they are not even close to what Intel delivers when it comes to IPC and single core performance. Thats why you struggle to keep a decent framerate with a good midrange PC that would run any other game on high settings. But even with my overclocked i9 I totally agree when you say we need multicore support in this application. And they should hard lock dynamic bones(and other stuff) to a very low level. And since it is an open sandbox and everyone can upload his/her own stuff it is not the fault of the devs that 95% of the avatars perform worse than some unoptimized games. With 4-5 unoptimized avatars in the box you cant blame the devs or the world for bad performance. It is all the crap going on with the avatars. They cost more performance than most modern AAA titles on ultra settings cause too many people do not care to optimize. I see it every day. Doesn't matter to what world I go if there are 10+ people in front of a mirror I have to block 2-4 of the worst rated and my fps are back to something that does not give me motion sickness. So stop throwing rocks at the devs and instead try to convince the players to optimize the avatars they use or to not use bad performing shit from random worlds.

That was not the intention of my post. And I am sure I'm not the only one who thinks there are too many poorly optimized avatars out there. And it is not an insult to say AMD has poor single core performance. I am not a fan of Intels security flaws and the price is beyond good and evil but I chose it because I think it is the best CPU for VRC and some emulators for example at the moment. That may change as soon as VRChat gets proper multicore optimization. If facts are insulting you I can't help with that. And it is imho not the Devs job to optimize poor worlds and avatars. Optimizing avatars does imho not mean to be less creative. Not optimizing them is on the other hand just lazy....

Users with similar specs average around 80FPS overall. Are you sure something else isn't going on?

I'd check into GPU driver updates-- and if you're on a laptop with a dual GPU, ensure you're running with the dedicated GPU, and not the integrated. I'd also suggest checking your GPU/CPU utilization while VRChat is running.

Additionally, if you're using a VR headset, make sure the headset's video connection is connected to your graphics card, not your motherboard.

I'll be closing this thread, as this is a support issue, not a Feature Request or Bug Report. I'd suggest contacting our Support team!

Please contact our Support team at http://help.vrchat.com/new (select the "SUP" category) and report your issue there. Please include as much information as possible, such as game logs, screenshots, and etc. Video is also very helpful, if applicable.
See posted note. This is a support issue, not a Bug Report or Feature Request.
